theorem.statement: For every admitted raw goal/context, the Brain's general decision controller must terminate each control step in exactly one authority-safe class: independently authenticated adequate action/realization, acquisition of the cheapest declared policy-changing information edge, explicit open/abstain with the exact missing authority edge, or fail-closed invalidity. No unsupported action is promoted to success.
theorem.robust_adequacy_law: A candidate policy is admissible only when its authenticated adequacy covers every surviving sound semantic/world model consistent with bound evidence and load-bearing constraints.
theorem.information_law: Information may be acquired only through an authenticated discriminator whose possible outcomes can change the admissible-policy set; otherwise it is decision-irrelevant and must not be requested.
theorem.execution_law: Effectful execution requires an authenticated selected-policy-to-execution binding or an exact grounded realization cell.
theorem.acceptance_law: Execution/effect success never self-certifies the user's goal. Actual goal satisfaction requires an independent content-addressed acceptance binding over the raw goal, selected policy/realization, observed result, and load-bearing constraints.

root_reclassification.reason: The remaining incompleteness is coverage of authenticated semantics, adequacy certificates, world predicates, execution bindings, and acceptance verifiers. It is not a missing general control-loop mechanism.

impossibility_boundary.claim: No finite controller can truthfully guarantee complete verified action adequacy over the unrestricted useful open world when materially different success/failure worlds can expose identical retained evidence, or when required semantic/goal predicates are not independently observable or decidable.
impossibility_boundary.consequence: Universal open-world coverage must remain an expandable verified frontier. The correct universal property is total fail-closed control, not omniscient semantic completeness.
impossibility_boundary.explanation: The original goal remains exact: take the right action. The controller executes only where that claim is evidenced; everywhere else it returns the exact information/authority gap instead of substituting a weaker success claim.
